Welcome to the **Isogeny Cryptography Wiki**. This site serves as an open-source, mathematically rigorous, and accessible repository of knowledge detailing post-quantum cryptographic protocols built on the hardness of finding isogenies between elliptic curves.

---

## Getting Started

If you are new to isogeny-based cryptography, we recommend exploring the protocols based on their underlying mathematical frameworks:

### Commutative Group Actions
Protocols built on the framework of Couveignes, Rostovtsev, and Stolbunov (CRS), utilizing commutative group actions on supersingular elliptic curves:

* **[CSIDH](protocols/csidh.qmd)** – Commutative Supersingular Isogeny Diffie-Hellman (Key Exchange).
* **[CSI-FiSh](protocols/csi-fish.qmd)** – Efficient signatures using the Fiat-Shamir transform over a known class group.

---

## Contributing

This wiki is maintained by the **isogeny-crypto** organization. If you spot a mathematical error, want to expand on a protocol's performance metrics, or wish to add a new primitive:

1. Fork the repository on [GitHub](https://github.com/isogeny-crypto/isogeny-crypto.github.io).
2. Create your article using a `.qmd` file in the `protocols/` directory.
3. Submit a Pull Request.
